title: Procedural Compliance and Enforcement at Custom Houses
summary: This thread covers the evolution of procedural requirements for goods clearance, audit, and dispute resolution involving Custom Houses.

evolution.procedure: Shifted from basic clearance notification to structured audit-based compliance and formal dispute resolution timelines.

timeline.change: Established a 10-day notice period for importers/exporters before forfeiture of goods.
Formalized the Transaction Based Audit (PCA) process initiated by Custom House commissioners.

৫। আমদানিকারক বা রপ্তানিকারক বা দাবীদারকে নোটিশ প্রদান:
আমদানিকৃত বা রপ্তানিকৃত পণ্য Customs Act, 1969 এর সংশ্লিষ্ট ধারার বিধান অনুযায়ী নির্ধারিত সময়ে খালাস নেয়া বা রপ্তানি করা না হলে উক্ত পণ্য রাষ্ট্রের অনুকূলে বাজেয়াপ্তির পূর্বে সংশ্লিষ্ট আমদানিকারক বা রপ্তানিকারককে পণ্য খালাস নেয়ার বা রপ্তানি করার জন্য অথবা চোরাচালানের অভিযোগে আটক ও জমাকৃত পণ্যের দাবীদার থাকলে উক্ত দাবীদারকে তাঁর দাবী প্রতিষ্ঠার সুযোগ প্রদানের জন্য ১০ (দশ) কার্যদিবস সময় প্রদান করে নোটিশ জারি করতে হবে। আল- মেনিফেস্টেড পণ্যচালানের ক্ষেত্রে শিপিং এজেন্ট বা বাহক বরাবরে এবং পণ্যের মালিকের ঠিকানা জানা না থাকলে সংশ্লিষ্ট কাস্টম হাউস বা কমিশনারেটের নোটিশ বোর্ডে নোটিশ টাঙ্গাতে হবে। আমদানিকৃত বা রপ্তানিকৃত পণ্যের ক্ষেত্রে উক্ত নোটিশ সংশ্লিষ্ট সিএন্ডএফ এজেন্ট এবং লিয়েন ব্যাংককেও প্রদান করতে হবে।

Customs Act 1969: This act governs the timeframes and legal requirements for the clearance and export of goods through customs.
Import and Export Clearance: Before goods are confiscated by the state due to failure to clear them within the prescribed time, the customs authority must issue a notice to the relevant importer, exporter, or claimant.
The notice provides a ten-working-day period for the importer or exporter to complete the clearance process or for a claimant to establish their claim over seized goods.
Customs Authority: The authority is required to serve notice to importers, exporters, or claimants before initiating confiscation proceedings.

In cases involving unmanifested goods, the authority must issue the notice to the shipping agent or carrier, and if the owner is unknown, post the notice on the official notice board of the relevant Custom House or Commissionerate.
Customs Clearing and Forwarding Agent: The customs clearing and forwarding agent must be served with the official notice regarding the clearance or export status of the imported or exported goods.
Lien Bank: The lien bank must be included in the notification process concerning the status of the imported or exported goods to ensure they are informed of pending confiscation or clearance actions.

Customs Act 1969: Section 83(C) of the Act serves as the legal basis for issuing official notices to conduct transaction-based audits on imported goods.
Transaction Based Audit: The Audit Team is responsible for conducting a transaction-based audit of specific bills of entry as directed by the Commissioner of Customs.

Auditees are required to present comprehensive documentation regarding their business profile, HS codes, declared values, concessional benefits, and compliance with import policies as part of the audit process.
Commissioner of Customs Valuation and In: This authority or the respective Custom House issues the official notice for the transaction-based audit and oversees the appointment of the audit team.
Import Registration Certificate: Auditees must provide details of their Import Registration Certificate, including its type, to verify their status as industrial or commercial importers.
VAT Compliant: The auditee must submit information confirming their VAT registration status and overall VAT compliance as part of the audit documentation requirements.
H.S. Code: The audit requires verification of declared HS codes against import documents, LCs, and the Bangladesh Customs Tariff, as well as checking against any advance rulings provided by the National Board of Revenue.
National Board of Revenue: The board is responsible for issuing advance rulings on HS codes and granting special concessions or privileges that are subject to review during a customs audit.
Customs Procedure Code: The audit examines concessional benefits claimed under various SROs or special orders to ensure that the appropriate Customs Procedure Code conditions have been satisfied, such as the installation of imported capital machinery.

192 G. Duration of Negotiation and Resolution.- (1)Whether pending or new dispute if the application submitted for ADR relates to the same Customs House or Station, all formalities mentioned in this chapter including the negotiation and agreement or disagreement or resolution, as the case may be, of the dispute, are to be completed in a period of maximum thirty working days from the date of submission of the application.
(2) For a pending dispute for which application is submitted to the Commissioner Appeal or Customs and VAT Appellate Tribunal or any Court, the duration for the above purposes will be sixty working days from the date of submission of the application.

Alternative Dispute Resolution: The process of dispute resolution through application must be completed within a specified timeframe of working days from the date the application is submitted.
For disputes originating at the same Custom House or Station, a maximum duration of thirty working days is allotted for completing all formalities including negotiation, agreement, or resolution.

For disputes that are already pending before the Commissioner (Appeals), the Customs, Excise and VAT Appellate Tribunal, or a Civil Court, an extended duration of sixty working days is provided for completing the resolution process.
Customs House: When an application for dispute resolution relates to a specific Custom House or Station, the time limits for completing the negotiation and resolution process are strictly enforced.
Commissioner (Appeals): If a dispute is pending before this authority, a longer period of sixty working days is granted for the resolution process to be completed following the submission of an application.
Customs, Excise and VAT Appellate Tribun: For disputes pending before this tribunal, the legal framework provides a sixty-day working period for the resolution process upon the submission of an application.
Civil Court: In cases where a dispute is pending before a Civil Court, the duration for completing the Alternative Dispute Resolution process is set at sixty working days from the application submission date.

Customs, Excise and VAT Appellate Tribun: Customs, Excise and VAT Appellate Tribunal
